clue.text: Holding up the Dark Lady's hat, giving remodelling

indicators.note: remodelling something rebuilds it in a new shape, so the preceding words are rearranged

blocks.note: the fourteen letters taken as written, ignoring punctuation

explanation.surface: Someone at a party is propping up the hat of Shakespeare's Dark Lady while making a fashion makeover.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dark Lady of Shakespeare's sonnets is a red herring; the definition reads 'holding up the dark', meaning delaying nightfall by putting the clocks forward.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving clocks forward an hour in summer postpones evening darkness, keeping evenings brighter for longer.

clue.text: With the French badly clued and in doubt, Switzerland might make a change

indicators.note: done badly means done wrong, so the next word's letters are disordered
placed in something means put inside it, so these pieces go within the doubt

blocks.note: le is French for the
the word clued rearranged
taken as written
CH is the international code for Switzerland, from Confoederatio Helvetica

explanation.surface: Confusing French clues leave a Swiss solver uncertain enough to change their mind.
explanation.walkthrough: The change is a gear change: in old cars without synchromesh, drivers declutched twice to shift.
explanation.definitionFit: Pressing the clutch twice during a gearchange matched engine speed on older cars, so a driver did this to shift gear.

clue.text: Putting up a grand chimney. Yes! With a lid for the synagogue

indicators.note: in a down entry, putting up lifts the letters so they read from the bottom

blocks.note: taken as written
a grand is a thousand, and K stands for a thousand
lum is the Scottish word for a chimney
ay is an old and dialect form of yes

explanation.surface: Someone building a fine chimney cheers, then turns to a hat worn at worship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lid' is slang for a hat; this is a variant spelling of yarmulke.
explanation.definitionFit: A yarmulke is the small skullcap worn by Jewish men, especially during prayer, and lid is slang for headwear.

clue.text: Do not, in any wise, speak of Edith Wharton's age

indicators.note: to speak something is to say it out loud, so the sound counts and not the spelling

blocks.note: not doing it in any way means doing it in no sense

explanation.surface: An instruction never to mention how old the novelist Edith Wharton was.
explanation.walkthrough: Edith Wharton wrote 'The Age of Innocence', so her 'age' is the one in that title, not her years.
explanation.definitionFit: Wharton's Pulitzer-winning novel is titled The Age of Innocence, so that word names her famous era.

clue.text: I hear two wise heads cracked with the times of their lives

indicators.note: what is heard is a sound, so the next words stand for letters that are pronounced that way
something cracked is broken apart, so these letters are reassembled

blocks.note: wise is said like the plural of the letter Y
taken as written

explanation.surface: A pair of sages have their heads broken in the prime of life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Two wise heads' reads as two sages, but wise is two Y letters by sound and heads is the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: One's prime years, when success and vigour peak, are the best periods anyone experiences.

clue.text: Low cloud's way over desert country

blocks.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
to rat is to desert one's side
the United States

explanation.surface: A cloud drifts low on its path over an arid desert land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desert' wants to be the sandy noun; here it is the verb meaning to abandon.
explanation.definitionFit: Stratus is a flat grey sheet of cloud forming at low altitude, often bringing drizzle.

clue.text: Without it a guest might lose face!

definitions.text: Without it a guest might lose face!

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the next word is taken out of the visitor

blocks.note: taken as written, the letters removed
a visitor is a guest

explanation.surface: A warning that a visitor could be embarrassed without some protection.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: a knight or welder without this guard risks injury to the face, and 'lose face' plays on embarrassment.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the movable front piece of a helmet or cap that shields the eyes and features.

clue.text: Resurgent racist borne on a zimmer frame

indicators.note: a frame holds something inside it, so the answer sits within the words before

blocks.note: the letters run across the words, from the end of borne to the start of zimmer

explanation.surface: An elderly racist, revived, is carried along on a walking frame.
explanation.walkthrough: A zimmer frame is a walking frame used by the elderly; 'frame' doubles as the container of the hidden letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A modern follower of Hitler's ideology is a revived fascist, a racist of a new generation.

clue.text: He helps me to sip with the Devil!

indicators.note: with here suggests the letters go along together and get mixed into a new order

blocks.note: the fourteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A tempter offers to share a drink, suggesting a pact with Satan.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal is weak; the exclamation mark hints that the letters themselves are bedevilled.
explanation.definitionFit: Mephistopheles is the demon of the Faust legend, to whom Faust sells his soul, a form of Satan.

clue.text: Not so virile as Gerard Hopkins, say?

indicators.note: say asks us to speak the description aloud, so it counts for its sound rather than its spelling

blocks.note: the poet Gerard Manley Hopkins with his middle name missing, so he is un-Manleyed

explanation.surface: A cheeky question about whether the Victorian poet Gerard Manley Hopkins was lacking in manliness.
explanation.walkthrough: The poet's full name is Gerard Manley Hopkins; written as just Gerard Hopkins, he has lost his Manley.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking the qualities traditionally thought masculine means weaker or less virile in character.

clue.text: Send back Swedish settler after the others

indicators.note: coming after the others means the coin is placed second, following the remainder

blocks.note: the rest means the others, the remainder
the ore is a small Swedish coin, something used to settle a bill

explanation.surface: A Swedish settler is shipped home once the rest of the colonists have gone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settler' suggests a colonist, but here it means a coin that settles a debt; the ore is one hundredth of a Swedish krona.
explanation.definitionFit: To give something back to its owner or former place is to return or reinstate it.

clue.text: Bloomer one's seen during return visit to the Old Vicarage

indicators.note: something seen during an event sits inside it, so one piece goes within another
a return trip goes back the way it came, so the next word is read backwards

blocks.note: the Roman numeral for one
a call is a short visit, here to the house in Rupert Brooke's poem

explanation.surface: On a return trip to Rupert Brooke's Old Vicarage, someone spots a flower in bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: Brooke's poem 'The Old Vicarage, Grantchester' opens with the line about this shrub being in bloom, so the reference is apt.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloomer is anything that flowers, and this shrub is known for fragrant purple or white flowers.

clue.text: A loud and complicated matter with hard consequences

definitions.note: plural in the clue; the answer is a singular noun for the consequences as a whole

indicators.note: a complicated thing is tangled up, so the next word's letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written
f is forte, the musical direction for loud
the word matter rearranged
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A noisy, messy business has tough repercussions afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The aftermath of an event is the period of results and effects that follow it, usually unpleasant ones.

clue.text: Finding out by practice

blocks.note: surface reading: learning something through repeated experience
setter's reading: a medical practice, where a doctor's finding about an illness is made

explanation.walkthrough: 'Practice' looks like repetition, but it is a doctor's surgery; the 'finding' is a medical one.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor's identification of an illness from its symptoms is the medical finding reached at a practice.

clue.text: Composer of Wordsworth's "Solitude"

blocks.note: first meaning: Sir Arthur ..., the English composer and Master of the Queen's Music
second meaning: Wordsworth's daffodils flash upon the inward eye

explanation.surface: Someone asks who set a Wordsworth poem called Solitude to music.
explanation.walkthrough: There is no such song; the quotation is from 'I Wandered Lonely as a Cloud', where the inward eye is 'the bliss of solitude'.
explanation.definitionFit: Arthur Bliss was a twentieth-century English composer, and Wordsworth calls the remembered daffodils the joy of being alone.

clue.text: I produce a pipe? That's right, with wife and family around

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the family wraps about the other pieces

blocks.note: i.e. is id est, that is
R is the abbreviation for right
W is the abbreviation for wife
a brood is a family of young

explanation.surface: A man fills his pipe at home, surrounded by his wife and children, and asks for agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's' is i.e., not a link; the answer speaks for itself in 'I produce a pipe'.
explanation.definitionFit: The root of the heath tree is carved into tobacco pipes, so this timber yields one.

clue.text: Such TV has us in stitches

definitions.note: plural in the clue; the answer is one kind of knitting stitch

blocks.note: first meaning: television delivered by wire rather than broadcast
second meaning: a twisted, rope-like knitting stitch

explanation.surface: A television comedy that has the viewers laughing helplessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In stitches' means laughing hard, but the stitches are a knitter's: a jumper can be worked in this rope-pattern stitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Subscription television comes down a wire, and knitters twist stitches into a raised rope pattern of the same name.

clue.text: Spending one's time in a punch-up: it would be boring

indicators.note: spending time in somewhere means being inside it, so the period goes within the fight

blocks.note: a brawl is a rough fight
AD, anno domini, is our era, one's time

explanation.surface: Someone who spends their time getting into fistfights must lead a dull life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' sounds like dull; the tool makes holes.
explanation.definitionFit: A small pointed hand tool used to make holes in wood for screws is something that bores.

clue.text: Accompaniment variations "al Tito Gobbi"? Not it!

indicators.note: musical variations rework a theme, so the quoted letters are rearranged
saying not this means leaving it out, so the following word is removed from the quotation

blocks.note: the letters of the quotation as written
taken as written, the letters to remove

explanation.surface: A piece of music billed as variations in the style of the Italian baritone Tito Gobbi, but not that.
explanation.walkthrough: Tito Gobbi was a famous Italian opera baritone, which keeps the musical surface intact.
explanation.definitionFit: An obbligato is an instrumental part that accompanies a vocal line, often an essential one.

clue.text: Full of vigour, but not perhaps hot on self-confidence

indicators.note: perhaps signals one possible version of a word, so its letters may be rearranged

blocks.note: the word not rearranged
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps
ego is one's sense of self-worth

explanation.surface: An energetic person who is nonetheless not much into self-assurance.
explanation.definitionFit: Being constantly busy and active describes someone energetic, bustling around with plenty of energy.

clue.text: Poop of vessel involved in battle

indicators.note: involved in means wrapped up inside, so the vessel sits within the battle

blocks.note: an urn is a vessel
a bout is a fight or contest

explanation.surface: The stern deck of a ship caught up in a naval engagement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poop' looks like the raised deck at a ship's stern, but here it is the verb to tire out, as in pooped.
explanation.definitionFit: To poop out is to become exhausted, and to exhaust oneself through overwork is the same.

clue.text: Declare a draw with Samson, for one?

blocks.note: taken as written
D is the abbreviation for drawn in results tables
Samson was one of the judges who led Israel in the Book of Judges

explanation.surface: A referee announces a tied result in a fight involving the strongman Samson.
explanation.walkthrough: Samson suggests a strongman, but in the Bible he is one of the Judges of Israel.
explanation.definitionFit: To pronounce or rule something formally, as a court does, is to declare it officially.

clue.text: Almost unable to construct a register the wrong way. Capital!

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the next word loses its final letter
to construct is to build anew, so the shortened letters are rearranged
going the wrong way means running backwards, so the register is read from its end

blocks.note: taken as written
a rota is a roster or list of duties

explanation.surface: Someone nearly fails to compile a list, gets it backwards, and is cheered with an exclamation of approval.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital!' sounds like an old-fashioned cry of 'splendid!', but it is the definition: a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: This older spelling names the capital city of Mongolia, now usually written Ulaanbaatar.

clue.text: Explosive expletive

definitions.note: adjective in the clue; the answer is the noun for an explosion

blocks.note: first meaning: an explosion or burst of air
second meaning: a mild curse of annoyance

explanation.surface: An angry outburst of swearing.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a detonation and is also a mild oath muttered in irritation.

clue.text: Prince of Hearts demands a drink. It's his round!

indicators.note: round suggests turning about, so the whole sequence is read backwards

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for hearts in card games
taken as written
a jar is British slang for a drink, usually a pint

explanation.surface: The Prince of Hearts calls for a drink in the pub, since it is his turn to buy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's his round' sounds like pub talk about buying drinks, but round here means turn the letters around.
explanation.definitionFit: A rajah is an Indian king or prince, a ruler of a princely state.

clue.text: Travesty when actions speak louder than words

definitions.text: when actions speak louder than words

blocks.note: first meaning: an absurd pretence or sham

blocks.clueFragment: when actions speak louder than words
blocks.note: second meaning: the parlour game in which players mime a word or title

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reworks the proverb: in the guessing game players must act and may not speak.
explanation.definitionFit: An absurd sham is a pretence, and the party game has teams miming syllables for others to guess.

clue.text: Oblate loves valid convert

indicators.note: to convert something changes its form, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, written as O, so two of them
taken as written

explanation.surface: A lay member of a religious order loves a genuine new recruit to the faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oblate' and 'convert' both suggest religion, but oblate is the geometric adjective for a flattened sphere.
explanation.definitionFit: An oblate body is squashed at the poles, roughly egg-shaped, so it can be described as rounded and elongated.

clue.text: Heavy-handed state of "le fast food" sent wild

indicators.note: something gone wild is out of control, so the letters before it are scrambled

blocks.note: the fourteen letters taken as written

explanation.surface: The French fast-food craze has driven someone into a heavy, clumsy frenzy.
explanation.definitionFit: Being clumsy, plodding and lacking finesse is a heavy-handed condition, unable to react with agility.
